name: ZH bialgebra
summary: A standard H-box connected to an X-spider becomes a complete bipartite graph of Z-spiders and H-boxes.
description:
The ZH analogue of the [bialgebra rule](../bialgebra-generalised/). An H-box connected to a phase-free X-spider is equal to a complete bipartite graph, where every leg of the H-box gets a Z-spider and every leg of the X-spider gets an H-box.

Classically this expresses that the AND gate and the COPY gate form a bialgebra, just like XOR and COPY: taking the AND and then copying the result is the same as copying both inputs and taking the ANDs pairwise. A special case is that an X-state (a $|0\rangle$) [explodes an H-box](../zh-h-box-zero-state-copy/).
parameter_notes: n legs on the H-box and m on the X-spider (shown for n = m = 2); holds for any numbers of legs.
notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
